speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, please describe your abdominal pain: where exactly is it located, what does it feel like, and when did it start? Also, have you experienced any nausea, vomiting, fever, or changes in your bowel movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ischemic Colitis (secondary to acute myocardial infarction). The combination of sudden periumbilical pain, bloody loose stools, and a recent cardiac event strongly suggests bowel ischemia due to hypoperfusion. I will order a CT angiogram of the abdomen to confirm bowel viability and rule out other causes. REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Angiography
